must_remember: Moment of inertia $I = \sum m_i r_i^2$ acts as the rotational analogue of mass in linear motion and has dimensions $[ML^2]$.
Theorem of Perpendicular Axes ($I_z = I_x + I_y$) is strictly applicable only to two-dimensional planar laminar bodies.
Theorem of Parallel Axes ($I = I_{cm} + Md^2$) is universally applicable to any rigid body of any shape.
Radius of gyration $k = \sqrt{I/M}$ represents the root-mean-square distance of mass distribution from the axis of rotation.

glossary.meaning: The measure of a body's resistance to angular acceleration about a given axis of rotation, defined by $\sum m_i r_i^2$ or $\int r^2 dm$.
The root-mean-square distance of the constituent mass particles from the axis of rotation, given by $k = \sqrt{I/M}$.
A two-dimensional flat object whose thickness is negligible, allowing the application of the perpendicular axes theorem.
Eigenvalues of the inertia tensor representing moments of inertia along principal axes where products of inertia vanish.
